summary:
I read everything and ran nothing (no builds, tests, cargo or main-run.sh calls). The notes file holds 20 findings with sources and four answer blocks for the drafter.

The four answers in short:
1. **Diagnostic loop.** Build with check.mjs's own bites command plus --no-run. Run the npt_net-ed8673eeeaf4db12 binary whole, 300 times (2 parallel loops of 150), through main-run.sh. That is about 90 minutes, with about a 95 % chance of seeing the failure again at a 1-in-97 rate. Caveat: the unchanged code can only show the failure again, not its cause. The check only counts and keeps no state, so confirming the cause needs a probe or a test that builds the state on purpose.
2. **The fix's evidence.** That test (S never reads) plus three plants that each fail every run. A cheap check that no non-test code changed: the npt-lab release sha256 stays 98c3967e…. The counted check.mjs bar is 552+a / 632+a tests. CHECK-NFF-1 stays out.
3. **Disk.** The worst case leaves about 3,720 MiB, under the 4,096 floor, so U4f's counted run would stop. Packing u4r-B1-64f3307d5c7f (821 MiB, about 600 back) before the counted run fixes it, but only if R4's precondition holds.
4. **Steps.** From plan to the advisor's head check, about 4 hours.

Two traps in the obvious commands:
- te_m3_loop.sh's `-p npt-net` build makes a different binary (301de27).
- Its `tail -1` would pick npt_tcpinfo in a workspace build.

Two things the existing records get wrong:
- The card's example plant would not bite reliably in the failing test.
- The advisor's ruling says npt-lab does not depend on npt-net; it does, through npt-server and npt-bots.
findings: F1 The bites test build is `cargo test --locked --workspace --all-features`, run from spikes/netcode-proof (check.mjs:2057); the measured build is `cargo test --locked --workspace` (:2053). Neither uses --no-fail-fast. main-run.sh exports CARGO_TARGET_DIR=.gate/shared-target (main-run.sh:15,18) and the profile is `test` (merge.log:26). The failing binary was .gate/shared-target/debug/deps/npt_net-ed8673eeeaf4db12 (merge.log:48).

F2 `cargo test --locked --workspace --all-features --no-run` gives that same ed8673 binary (u4r/c6-end3.log:65,105; te2-5/run1.log). The hash depends on features and profile, not on the source (it is the same at 9e0f103 and 561bf42). The measured build's npt-net is 088534cbcaf56b90 (c6-end3.log:43).

F3 (trap) `cargo test -p npt-net --lib --all-features`, as in te_m3_loop.sh:25, builds a different binary, npt_net-301de27e05915ce7. It leaves out npt-l1's `bites` feature (crates/l1/Cargo.toml:12-15) and the other members' feature unification. TE-M3's 80 loop runs used that binary, not check.mjs's.

F4 (trap) A workspace --no-run build prints 30 'Executable unittests src/lib.rs' lines, and the last one is npt_tcpinfo's (c6-end3.log:63). te_m3_loop.sh:28 (`tail -1`) would pick it. The new loop must match `npt_net-` and stop unless the name is npt_net-ed8673eeeaf4db12.

F5 One run of the whole ed8673 binary (169 passed, 12 ignored) takes 29.43-31.05 s across 14 kept runs (te2-5/run1-10.log and 4 u4r regression logs). With 2 parallel loops it is about 18 s a run overall (te-m3/loop.log:4-18; card :2973: 60 runs from 11:47 to 12:05).

F6 Basis for N: 1 failure (merge.log:51) against 14 kept ed8673 passes, 81 kept 301de27 passes and the bites half of about 54 check.mjs test steps kept only as summary lines. That is 1 in 97 (the advisor's count) to 1 in 150. The chance of seeing it again in 300 runs is 95.5 % at 1 in 97 and 86.6 % at 1 in 150. 300 runs with no failure bounds the rate under 1 %.

F7 check_held_bound (delay.rs:521-544) only counts; it keeps no state of the sample that counted. The test's println (delay_tests.rs:2292-2299) shows only the counts and the largest excess. So a loop of the unchanged code can reproduce the failure, but it cannot by itself confirm the release-pending state that the cause names.

F8 (plant reach) In the failing test the client drains a 1 MB duplex (delay_tests.rs:2268-2274), so released_model is about 0 at most writes. The card's plant (drop released_model from down_free, delay.rs:473-477) would then bite only inside the same rare window. It bites every run only where S never reads (duplex(1_024), as in delay_tests.rs:745-747). In that existing test, though, the plant would first fail the Pending assertion (:779-782), and a 100 B write stays under 64 KB, so the bound check would not be the failing line either.

F9 (design discriminator) A fix that checks 'held minus the released-but-untaken bytes <= 64 KB + prefix' at every sample cannot catch the card's plant: admission still keeps outstanding <= 64 KB, and all the extra bytes are released and untaken. Only a check of the whole held at each write (netcode-architect F7 and F10) catches it. So the plant also tests the fix's design, not only its wiring.

F10 (deterministic cause) With S never reading and P2 loss: the writer back-fills a front record's acknowledged prefix, that record is then released and never taken, and held stays above 64 KB + the new front's prefix. The old every-sample check then counts on every run. A test built this way, run against the old check as a plant, confirms the cause with no race involved.

F11 The advisor's merge-stop ruling (advisor-c62h-bound-merge-stop-full.json:3) says npt-lab does not depend on npt-net. That is true directly but false transitively: crates/lab/Cargo.toml:30,32 bring in npt-server and npt-bots, which depend on npt-net (crates/server/Cargo.toml:29, crates/bots/Cargo.toml:25), and merge-2.log:43 compiles npt-net for the npt-lab release build. C62H-BOUND's conclusion is unaffected (its lane did not change crates/net). Low.

F12 A cheap check that the fix touches only test code: the npt-lab release sha256 98c3967e04e4260985d24173b1fb2126ea1444636f4725e12cf76333d90b5113 (preflight.log) was the same in both build caches (u4r-report.md:1589). The spike tree outside results/ is unchanged from ea08f89 to HEAD (git diff --quiet exits 0).

F13 The counts are unchanged since 561bf42 (git diff --stat prints nothing): 552 measured / 632 bites tests (merge-2.log:12), refs 1350 tracked files and redact 305 items (main-54/light.log:5,8), marks 81, self 78 of 78.

F14 Disk: 4,951 MiB free at 07:29 (light.log:2) and 4,993 MiB by df at about 08:10. A whole check.mjs run used 1,022 MiB net at worst (counted-merge-2.log:2 and card :373) and freed 804 MiB at best (merge-2.log:2 and :23). A bites test build costs 16-33 MiB net. The shared target is warm: 6,308 MiB, of which incremental is 2,979.

F15 Brief 8.1's packing order is u4r-P2-ab10f058a828 (already packed, 572 MiB back; card :4009-4017), then u4r-B1-64f3307d5c7f (821 MiB), then u4r-P3-0f066338dd8d (519 MiB). R4 excludes both P0 folders, fc411116c1f1, fd4612050cd6 and the two c-u2 folders. u4r-P2-8ee453c22882 and u4r-P3-d66e23cd78f2 are not on 8.1's list.

F16 R4 (card :197, :202-203) says 'Nothing is packed before he has read it', and the card's line 10 at 07:38 UTC still says it is waiting for his answers. 8.1 is also written for 'Before each set' of C62H-BOUND's sets (c62h-bound-brief.md:489).
proposal:
1. DIAGNOSTIC (code unchanged)
- The main session writes .checkpoints/netcode-proof-test/u3c-held-1/u3c_held_loop.sh, a copy of te_m3_loop.sh with these changes:
  - It builds with `cargo test --locked --workspace --all-features --no-run`.
  - It takes BIN from the line matching `/npt_net-[0-9a-f]{16}` and stops with exit 2 unless the name is npt_net-ed8673eeeaf4db12.
  - It runs sha256sum on delay.rs, delay_tests.rs and BIN.
  - Each run's line also carries the watched test's own result line (ok or FAILED).
  - On a failure it prints libtest's failures list and the test's `---- <name> stdout ----` block.
- The call: `bash /home/user/Shamble-Frontlines/.checkpoints/netcode-proof-test/main-run.sh /home/user/Shamble-Frontlines/.gate/u3c-held-1/l1.log df -B1 /home/user :: bash /home/user/Shamble-Frontlines/.checkpoints/netcode-proof-test/u3c-held-1/u3c_held_loop.sh l1 all 150 2 0 :: df -B1 /home/user`
  - That is N = 300, stopping at the first failure; about 1 minute of build plus about 90 minutes of runs.
- If L1 catches nothing, run L2: `u3c_held_loop.sh l2 one 300 2 6` (the test alone, --nocapture, 6 busy loops; this is how TE-M3 caught its failure).
- Reproduced means: the assert at delay_tests.rs:2300-2304 fails with [k>=1, 0], the excess is under 16,406 B, first losses are above 0, and nothing else fails.
- Confirmed means: every counted sample shows released_model[DOWN] > 0 and held at or below the last write's bound. This needs either a probe (an eprintln in check_held_bound, put in and taken out by Edit, with hashes, never committed) or T-NEW with plant P-a.
- Stop for the advisor if any of these happen:
  - the binary name is wrong;
  - another test fails, or this test fails on another line (:2283, :2305);
  - the UP count is above 0;
  - a counted sample has no released-untaken record, or held is above the last write's bound;
  - no failure in 300 runs, unless the plan review has already ruled that T-NEW with P-a carries the confirmation;
  - main-run.sh exits 3 (the disk floor).

2. THE FIX'S EVIDENCE
- E1: the old test keeps its exit conditions (records >= 100, beyond > 0, lost > 0) and :2305. It adds an assert that the write-time check ran at least `records` times.
- E2: T-NEW, where S never reads, on duplex(1_024) with P2 loss.
  - It waits with until(HANG), never with sleep.
  - It asserts the bound before any Pending assert.
  - An UP count assert goes in if a test has up traffic.
- E3: loops on the fixed code.
  - Mode one: 2 x 300 runs with 6 busy loops.
  - Mode all: 10 x 2 runs with 4 busy loops.
- E4: the plants. For each: sha256 before, Edit in, one main-run.sh call that builds the workspace bites tests and runs the whole ed8673 binary, then Edit back, the sha256 equal again, and `git diff --quiet HEAD -- spikes/netcode-proof/crates/net` exiting 0. Each plant must fail with exit 101 on the named line:
  - P-a: the old every-sample check put back. T-NEW must fail.
  - P-b: released_model dropped from down_free. T-NEW's bound assert must fail.
  - P-c: the check call removed from the down write site. The count assert must fail.
  - P-d: the same for UP, if E2 has an UP count.
- E5: `cargo build --locked --release -p npt-lab`; its sha256 must be 98c3967e…5113.
- E6: one counted main-run.sh call, `df :: node check.mjs :: df`, on the fixed head. Its pass bar, written before it runs:
  - Header: HEAD is the fixed head; diff and untracked hashes are both e3b0c442….
  - check.mjs exits 0 with "check: all 11 steps pass".
  - Tests: measured 552+a and bites 632+a, 0 failed, 0 skips (T-NEW alone gives 553 / 633).
  - refs: the head's `git ls-files` count. marks: 81. self: 78 of 78. redact: 10 of 10, with 305 items plus one per pack list. deps: 137 crate files.
  - wasm: 27000 ticks, 0 mismatching. Never pin the hash-map digests.
  - det-u4 and the hash check are not needed, because E5 covers them.
- E7: `node tools/gate.mjs --no-smoke` gives GATE PASS, then CI is green.
- CHECK-NFF-1 stays out. The rule: one change-set at a time, and a change carries only what its own claim needs to be proven. A Low never triggers a push on its own, and its taker is check.mjs's next owner (advisor C4).

3. DISK
- The worst case is about 1,230 MiB used (under 60 for the loops, about 150 for the rebuilds, up to 1,022 for the whole run). That leaves about 3,720 MiB, under 4,096, so U4f's counted run would stop.
- Every call in this change-set still starts above the floor.
- The bar: at least 5,220 MiB free at the start of E6. If below, pack after E5 and before E6, one folder at a time:
  - first u4r-B1-64f3307d5c7f (about 600 MiB back);
  - then, only if still short, u4r-P3-0f066338dd8d (about 380 back);
  - each by 8.1's procedure, citing advisor-u4r-sets-r2-full.md:45, and only after R4's precondition is confirmed.

4. ORDER AND REVIEWERS
1. Plan → the advisor's plan review.
2. L1, and L2 or the probe as ruled.
3. The fix, by Edit in the main folder.
4. E3 to E5, then the gate.
5. Commit on the spike branch.
6. One review round on the final diff: netcode-architect and test-engineer, plus rust-reviewer if the advisor reads CLAUDE.md step 5 that way. One fix pass, then E3 and E4 again on what changed.
7. Pack if the bar says so.
8. E6, E7, save the card (it pushes), CI.
9. The advisor's check of the pushed head, naming the full SHA. All of this before U4f's merge.

About 4 hours in all.
risks: The unchanged-code loop may not reproduce the failure in 300 runs (about a 5-14 % chance even if the cause is right). Without a probe or T-NEW, a catch confirms the symptom, not the release-transient cause, so the plan must say in advance which result counts as confirmation.

If the loop is built the TE-M3 way (-p npt-net), it tests a different binary than check.mjs (301de27 instead of ed8673). Copying te_m3_loop.sh's `tail -1` would silently pick npt_tcpinfo in a workspace build.

The card's example plant (drop released_model from down_free) may pass in the existing failing test, because released records are taken at once there. A plant that bites only sometimes proves nothing. It needs a test where S never reads, with the bound assert placed before the Pending assert.
A fix that subtracts released-untaken bytes from held at every sample would pass the old test but miss the card's plant (F9). The plant result decides between the designs.
T-NEW adds its own timing exposure (hang guard, release waits). It must wait with until(), never sleep, and be looped (E3) before it counts.

Disk: the worst case leaves about 3,720 MiB, under the floor, which stops U4f's counted run at main-run.sh:44-47. Packing may be blocked by R4's 'nothing is packed before he has read it' (card :203). Each pack list committed under results/ shifts redact's item count, so the pass bar must say so in advance.
The peak disk use during a run is not measured anywhere: main-run.sh checks the floor only at its start. Each call should carry df before and after.

The advisor's ruling says npt-lab does not depend on npt-net, which is false transitively. A plan that drops det-u4 and the hash check on that ground alone would rest on a wrong premise. E5's npt-lab hash is the sound ground.
open_questions: Does R4's precondition hold now (his reading of the report; card :10 still says waiting), and does brief 8.1, written for C62H-BOUND's sets, cover packing for U3C-HELD-1's counted run? The advisor rules on this in the plan review.

If L1 (and L2) catch nothing in 300 runs, is the cause confirmed by T-NEW with plant P-a (deterministic), or does the advisor want a probe run as well? This should be decided in the plan review, so it does not cost an extra round.

Is T-NEW feasible as described: P2 loss with S never reading, held above 64 KB at a write, then a front release that stays untaken? This is netcode-architect's design call. If not, which test gives the card's plant a bite every run?
Does the UP direction have a test that reaches its bound, so the write-time check at move_up gets its own count assert and plant (P-d)?
Does rust-reviewer join the review round? CLAUDE.md step 5 names it for Rust code; the card names only netcode-architect and test-engineer.

Should the advisor's sentence 'npt-lab does not depend on npt-net at all' (advisor-c62h-bound-merge-stop-full.json:3) be corrected on the card as a Low, so later plans do not drop det-u4 or the hash check on that ground?
